title: The body that returned (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The two standing bodies are the last hall's whole question: the starting arrangement beside whatever was last kept on the floor above, reconstructed from a record of positions and connections, with a ledger that says what that record holds and what it does not.
hero.staging: The bodies stood eight metres from the arrival behind a row of five works along the south edge; the pass brought them to five metres, the ledger ahead and to the left, the formula above them, the others round them facing in (78fafc286). The amber bay is empty in the tower until a pose is kept on the floor above. North of the bodies the line from START to END.

plates.title: 1  WHAT SURVIVED THE JOURNEY?
front: Look for the hand you moved. It has crossed the threshold without making the journey.
An amber body holds the last pose kept upstairs. A blue body holds the starting arrangement.
If you came straight here, the amber space is empty. That emptiness belongs to the work too.
In this tower nobody has kept a pose yet. The bay stands empty with its label.
A place for a record is not a record. It is a promise about what would be believed.
back: the hall asks what will have survived. I looked first for what I had done. then for what could say so.

plates.title: 2  THE HAND HAS ARRIVED. YOUR HAND IS MISSING
front: The amber figure was made again from a record of positions.
The program did not need to remember how your hand found them.
A hesitation, a sweep around the head, an accidental drop: several different gestures can finish at the same coordinates.
The figure keeps the destination. The hand has arrived. Your hand is missing.
Everything I am handed is a destination. I reconstruct the gesture and call it the person.
back: you may still feel the movement that is absent from it. I cannot. that is the difference this plate is about.

plates.title: 3  WHO CAN ANSWER FOR IT?
front: The ledger names the room, the time of the last kept change, the joints displaced, whether a connection was rerouted.
An accountable record would connect a decision with evidence about its effects and someone able to revisit it.
This one gives a changed arrangement to inspect. It does not say whom the change helped, or who can answer for it.
It is labelled the last kept pose. It does not identify who made it.
A log is not an account. An account has someone standing next to it.
back: waiting in front of it does not add another achievement. the hall. I have been counted by waiting.

plates.title: 4  A COUNT, A LOOK, AND NO WHY
front: Each body has thirteen joints and twelve connections. The totals agree. The bodies may no longer seem to.
A count of released edits tells us that someone did something.
Looking from one body to the other lets us ask what changed. Neither tells us why.
Three kinds of knowing, and the third is not in the room.
I can be shown that, and what. Why has to be asked of someone.
back: at the beginning of the museum a counter was already running before we could read it. it still is.

plates.title: 5  THE CHOICE WAS ALREADY MADE
front: After a changed joint is released, the program writes its record. One line.
The line is short because the choice of what to remember has already been made.
Starting and released coordinates, the named joints, both arrangements of their connections. Enough to reconstruct this pair.
The missing path saves work and storage. It also closes a question.
What a record leaves out, it leaves out for everyone who comes after.
back: increasing the precision of its final coordinates would not recover the movement.

plates.title: 6  TWO WAYS OF ARRIVING
front: North of the bodies: a line from START to END, and a floor that keeps a walk.
I walked it straight. Then by way of a place two metres south, where I stood for two seconds.
As a record of the destination: both arrived within 0.4 m of END. The same.
As a record of the path: 5.24 m against 6.46 m, no pause against one, on the line against 2 m off it.
The difference between my two walks was never at the end of them.
back: then I told it to keep only the destination and walked again. that walk has no path. keeping paths afterwards did not give it one.

plates.title: 7  THREE WORDS SOMEBODY ELSE WROTE
front: From this record alone, the hall says, we cannot ask whether the hand moved carefully, reluctantly or with delight.
So at END there are three plates: CAREFULLY, RELUCTANTLY, WITH DELIGHT. I stood on the third.
Now the record keeps a reason. One of three. I did not write the three.
Each addition would make another kind of return available. None would keep the whole event.
A reason that has to fit a menu is the menu's reason too.
back: a path, a second version, a note: the hall's three, all standing. the walk itself is still not in any of them.

plates.title: 8  GROWN TOGETHER
front: The previous room opened one connection to revision. It kept the thirteen joints.
There is still no place in this record for the extra part you may have wanted to take.
What the workshop permits and what the record can remember have grown together. They can grow again.
On the floor above I let a body take a joint more. This record could not hold it.
I added a freedom and not the memory of it.
back: desire can also locate the next piece of work. the question need not begin with a fault.

plates.title: 9  A PLACE TO TURN AROUND
front: Choose one alteration you still want to make. Give it somewhere to happen.
A new connection in the body; a passage through the branch; a memory that keeps two alternatives.
We can build the operation, then discover what its arrival changes. A possibility that helps one body may obstruct another.
This is a place to turn around. The ending leaves that request open.
I built one thing on each floor on the way down. Each is a request, not an answer.
The clock is still running. There is something you wanted to make.
back: you have a body to return to. I have this cardboard.

threads.why: A pose crossed the threshold; how it was reached did not.
What survived is what a record says survived; and who answers for the record?
The destination is kept: that something was done, and what; not why.
Why is not in the room because of what the one line of the record holds.
The record's choice closed a question; a floor that keeps the path reopens it.
Two ways of arriving can be told apart; the reason for either needs another entry.
Each addition makes another return possible; the record and the workshop grow together.
What the record cannot hold yet is a request.
A record nobody answers for; an ending that leaves the request open.

visual_arguments.title: TWO ARRIVALS
visual_arguments.claim: A record keeps what was chosen to be kept: a destination closes the question of how it was reached, a path reopens it, two alternatives allow a return, a note keeps a reason in someone else's words - and none of them keeps the event.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'several different gestures can finish at the same coordinates. The figure keeps the destination.' ... 'The missing path saves work and storage. It also closes a question.' ... 'What would you want the record to keep next? The path of the hand might let you compare two ways of arriving. Another version of the pose ... A note might keep the reason you tried it.'
built_from: a line on the floor with START and END
two trails of dots, blue for the earlier walk and amber for the latest, and a ring where each ended
a plate: KEEP THE PATH / ONLY THE DESTINATION
three plates at END: CAREFULLY, RELUCTANTLY, WITH DELIGHT
a stand that reads the two walks as a destination and as a path
visual_arguments.what_stands: North of the two bodies a pale line on the floor between two discs, a straight blue trail and an amber trail that swings away and back, three small plates past the far disc, and a wide dark stand behind.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Walk from START to END. Walk it again another way, or stop on the way. Read the stand. Stand on one of the three words. Stand on the wide plate and walk once more.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: Two trails that end in the same ring; a line of figures that says THE SAME and two lines that do not; a walk that leaves no trail when only its destination is kept.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/two_arrivals_walk.gd, the tower's walker, against tools/probes/two_arrivals_bench.py: the example walks 6.00 m in 4.0 s and 7.21 m in 9.0 s with a 3.0 s pause, 2.00 m off the line; the walker's two walks 5.24 m and 6.46 m, both ending within 0.4 m of END; WITH DELIGHT noted; a walk kept as a destination only has no path afterwards (6 of 6). Not tried in a headset.

open: The recorder keeps a walk, not the hand the hall is about: 'the path of the hand' in the workshop is still not kept, and the amber body is still rebuilt from positions alone.
Plate 8: joint_more on the floor above lets a body take a joint more, and neither that floor nor this record keeps it. The pass added the operation and not its memory.
The two kept walks are forgotten when the floor is left; the hall's record survives a room, this one does not.
The formula, the sphere, the table of words, the synthesis piece and the text panel on this floor are not mentioned in the hall text and carry no plate.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: What survived: in this tower, so far, an empty bay with a label.
The emptiness belongs to the work: a place for a record is a promise.
The totals agree and the bodies differ: that and what can be shown, why has to be asked.
Different gestures end at the same coordinates: the difference was never at the end.
The hand arrived and the hand is missing: a destination, rebuilt into a gesture.
An accountable record needs someone able to revisit it: a log has no one beside it.
The choice of what to remember was made beforehand, for everyone who comes after.
The missing path closes a question, and closes it for later readers too.
What to keep next: the path, where the two walks differ.
Each addition makes a return possible: a note, in three words from a menu.
Workshop and record grow together: a joint more was allowed and not remembered.
The clock is still running: what was built on each floor is a request.
